questions.text: The Planning Commission of India was replaced by NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) through a Cabinet resolution in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Government formation context. The new government assumed office in May 2014. NITI Aayog was established via resolution on January 1, 2015. Eliminate 2014 (transition year), 2016/2017 (later policy implementations like GST). Full Solution: The Planning Commission, established in 1950, was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015 through a Cabinet resolution. NITI Aayog serves as the premier policy 'Think Tank' of the Government of India, providing directional and policy inputs with a focus on cooperative federalism.

questions.text: As per the table below listing Viceroys of India and key events during their tenure, which Viceroy was associated with the Partition of Bengal (1905)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use chronological elimination. Partition of Bengal occurred in 1905. Check tenures: Lord Curzon (1899–1905) covers 1905. Lord Minto (1905–1910) started in 1905 but the decision/implementation is attributed to Curzon. Lord Hardinge (1910–1916) cancelled it in 1911. Lord Chelmsford (1916–1921) is too late. Worked Solution: The table shows Lord Curzon's tenure (1899-1905) includes the year 1905 when the Partition was effected. Lord Minto's tenure began in Nov 1905. Lord Hardinge annulled it in 1911. Lord Chelmsford is associated with the 1919 Reforms. Hence, Lord Curzon is the correct answer.

questions.text: Refer to the table showing the sectoral contribution to India's Gross Value Added (GVA) at current prices (approximate %) for the year 2022-23 (First Revised Estimates). Which sector had the second-highest share in GVA?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Services is always highest (~53-55%). Industry is consistently second (~25-30%). Agriculture is third (~15-18%). Construction is a sub-sector of Industry. Worked Solution: As per National Accounts Statistics 2024 for 2022-23 (FRE): Services ~54%, Industry ~26%, Agriculture ~15%, Construction ~8% (part of Industry). Industry is the second largest sector.

questions.text: The Battle of Buxar, which decisively established British supremacy in Bengal, was fought in the year:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Timeline elimination. 1757 is Battle of Plassey. 1761 is Third Battle of Panipat. 1765 is Treaty of Allahabad (post-Buxar). The battle itself occurred in 1764. Full Solution: The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764 between the forces of the British East India Company under Hector Munro and the combined armies of Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh), and Shah Alam II (Mughal Emperor). The British victory led to the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765.

questions.text: Night blindness is caused by the deficiency of which vitamin?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Mnemonic association 'A' for 'A' (Night Blindness/Retinol). Eliminate B1 (Beriberi), C (Scurvy), D (Rickets/Osteomalacia). Full Solution: Vitamin A (Retinol) is essential for the synthesis of rhodopsin, the visual pigment in the retina's rod cells responsible for low-light vision. Its deficiency leads to impaired dark adaptation known as night blindness (nyctalopia), and prolonged deficiency causes xerophthalmia and keratomalacia.

questions.text: The approximate speed of light in vacuum is a fundamental physical constant. Which of the following represents its standard value in SI units?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Unit Elimination & Magnitude Check. The standard SI unit for speed is m/s. Option A uses km/s (non-SI base unit, though magnitude 3x10^5 km/s is correct). Option D (3x10^8 km/s) is 1000x too large. Option C (3x10^6 m/s) is 100x too small. Option B (3x10^8 m/s) matches the exact SI definition (299,792,458 m/s ≈ 3x10^8 m/s). Worked Solution: The defined value of the speed of light in vacuum (c) is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second. For examinations, this is approximated as 3.0 × 10^8 m/s. Option A is dimensionally correct in magnitude but not the standard SI representation (metres). Option B is the standard textbook approximation in SI units.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the production of major food grains in India (Fourth Advance Estimates 2022-23), which crop had the second-highest production volume?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the known hierarchy of Indian food grain production: Rice > Wheat > Maize > Pulses. Rice is the highest (approx. 135 MT), so eliminate Option A. Wheat (approx. 110 MT) is roughly 3 times Maize (approx. 35 MT) and 4 times Pulses (approx. 26 MT), confirming it is second. Worked Solution: From the table, Rice = 135.76 MT (1st), Wheat = 110.55 MT (2nd), Maize = 35.91 MT (3rd), Total Pulses = 26.05 MT (4th). Comparing the values directly, Wheat has the second-highest production.

questions.text: Refer to the table showing the approximate lengths of major Indian rivers. Which river has the second-longest length entirely within India (or total length for transboundary rivers as per standard convention)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Ganga (Option D) immediately as it is the longest river in India (~2525 km). Among the remaining Peninsular rivers, the standard descending order of length is Godavari (~1465 km) > Krishna (~1400 km) > Yamuna (~1376 km). Option A (Godavari) is the only plausible answer for second place. Worked Solution: From the table, Ganga = 2525 km (1st), Godavari = 1465 km (2nd), Krishna = 1400 km (3rd), Yamuna = 1376 km (4th). Godavari is clearly the second longest.

questions.text: The decisive Battle of Talikota (1565 CE), which led to the catastrophic decline of the Vijayanagara Empire, was fought between the Vijayanagara forces and a confederacy of which powers?
questions.solution: Shortcut: **Talikota (1565)** is historically synonymous with the combined attack by the **Deccan Sultanates**. Use chronological elimination: Mughals (Akbar) were in North India; Marathas (Shivaji) rose ~70 years later; Portuguese were coastal; Cholas/Pandyas had declined by the 13th century. Only the Deccan Sultanates were the immediate powerful neighbours of Vijayanagara in the 16th century. Worked: The Battle of Talikota (also called Rakshasa-Tangadi) was fought on 23 January 1565 between the Vijayanagara Empire under Aliya Rama Raya and the united forces of the four major Deccan Sultanates: Hussain Nizam Shah I of Ahmadnagar, Ali Adil Shah I of Bijapur, Ibrahim Qutb Shah Wali of Golconda, and Ali Barid Shah I of Bidar. The defeat resulted in the sack of the capital Hampi and the end of Vijayanagara's imperial dominance.

questions.text: Refer to the table below showing important Constitutional Amendment Acts of India. Which Amendment Act reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Subject Association Elimination. 42nd Amendment (1976) is known as 'Mini Constitution' (Preamble, Fundamental Duties). 52nd Amendment (1985) introduced Anti-Defection Law (10th Schedule). 73rd Amendment (1992) constitutionalized Panchayati Raj. By elimination, 61st Amendment (1988) is the only one left for voting age reduction. Worked Solution: The table confirms the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (effective 1989) amended Article 326 to reduce the voting age from 21 to 18 years. The 42nd Amendment dealt with Parliament supremacy and Duties; the 52nd with Defection; the 73rd with Local Self Government.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is President's Rule imposed in a State due to the failure of constitutional machinery?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate Article 352 (National Emergency), Article 360 (Financial Emergency), and Article 365 (Failure to comply with Union directions). Article 356 specifically deals with the failure of constitutional machinery in states. Full Solution: Article 356 empowers the President to issue a proclamation if satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

questions.text: Which of the following plant hormones is primarily responsible for inducing dormancy in seeds and buds, and helps plants withstand water stress by triggering stomatal closure?
questions.solution: Shortcut: **Abscisic Acid (ABA)** -> Think **"Abscission" / "Abort" / "Anti-growth"**. It is the **stress hormone** (closes stomata during drought) and induces **dormancy**. The other three are primarily **growth promoters**: Auxin (cell elongation/apical dominance), Gibberellin (breaks dormancy/stem elongation), Cytokinin (cell division/delays senescence). Worked: Abscisic Acid (ABA) accumulates in leaves under water stress (drought), signaling guard cells to close stomata, reducing transpiration. It also enforces seed and bud dormancy by inhibiting germination/growth processes during unfavorable conditions (winter/drought), ensuring survival. Conversely, Gibberellins are known to *break* seed dormancy.

questions.text: Under Article 352 of the Constitution of India, a Proclamation of National Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within what period from the date of its issue?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The 44th Amendment (1978) reduced the parliamentary approval period for National Emergency (Art 352) from **2 months to 1 month**. Options "6 months" and "1 year" typically refer to the maximum duration for President's Rule (Art 356) extension or the period for which an approved Emergency can continue without fresh approval. Eliminate longer periods; the initial approval window is the shortest. Worked: Article 352 stipulates that a Proclamation of Emergency must be laid before each House of Parliament. It ceases to operate at the expiration of **one month** unless approved by resolutions of both Houses passed by a special majority. Prior to the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, this period was two months.

questions.text: As per the table showing the number of Ramsar Sites designated in India as of January 2024, categorized by state (Top 4 states), which state has the second-highest number of sites?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Direct data retrieval from table. Tamil Nadu (16) is highest. Uttar Pradesh (10) is second. Punjab (6) and Gujarat (4) follow. Worked Solution: The table explicitly lists Tamil Nadu with 16 sites, Uttar Pradesh with 10 sites, Punjab with 6 sites, and Gujarat with 4 sites. Ranking them: 1. Tamil Nadu, 2. Uttar Pradesh, 3. Punjab, 4. Gujarat. Uttar Pradesh is the correct answer.
